title: Agriculturist Licensure Examination (ALE)
disclaimer: Original practice items for educational simulation only. Not affiliated with PRC/CSC.

questions.subject: Crop Science
questions.stem: Photosynthesis in green crops primarily converts light energy into:
choices: Only heat with no organic product
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis produces carbohydrates as stored chemical energy.

questions.subject: Crop Science
questions.stem: In the Philippines, the staple cereal crop of greatest national importance is:
questions.explanation: Rice is the primary staple crop in the Philippines.

questions.subject: Crop Science
questions.stem: Hybrid vigor (heterosis) is commonly exploited to:
choices: Increase performance of offspring beyond parents for selected traits
questions.explanation: Heterosis can improve yield/traits in hybrid cultivars.

questions.subject: Soil Science
questions.stem: A soil with roughly equal sand, silt, and clay and good tilth is generally called:
questions.explanation: Loam is a balanced, workable agricultural soil texture class.

questions.subject: Soil Science
questions.stem: Most Philippine field crops prefer soils that are:
choices: Near neutral to slightly acidic, depending on crop
questions.explanation: Crop nutrient availability is generally better near neutral to slightly acidic conditions.

questions.subject: Soil Science
questions.stem: Nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium are known as:
questions.explanation: N, P, and K are primary plant macronutrients.

questions.subject: Crop Protection
questions.stem: IPM emphasizes:
choices: Calendar spraying only regardless of thresholds
Combining cultural, biological, and chemical tactics based on monitoring and thresholds
questions.explanation: IPM is an ecological, threshold-based multi-tactic approach.

questions.subject: Crop Protection
questions.stem: A plant disease epidemic typically requires a susceptible host, a virulent pathogen, and:
questions.explanation: The disease triangle: host, pathogen, and environment.

questions.subject: Crop Protection
questions.stem: Incomplete metamorphosis insects generally lack a distinct:
questions.explanation: Hemimetabolous insects lack a pupal stage.

questions.subject: Animal Science
questions.stem: Ruminants can utilize fibrous forages efficiently largely because of:
questions.explanation: Rumen microbes ferment fiber into usable products.

questions.subject: Animal Science
questions.stem: Broiler production primarily aims to raise chickens for:
questions.explanation: Broilers are meat-type chickens.

questions.subject: Animal Science
questions.stem: Selection of breeding animals should primarily consider:
questions.explanation: Genetic improvement relies on objective selection criteria.

questions.subject: Agricultural Economics and Marketing
questions.stem: Other factors constant, an increase in demand for mangoes tends to:
choices: Raise equilibrium price and/or quantity traded
questions.explanation: Higher demand shifts the demand curve rightward, raising price/quantity.

questions.subject: Agricultural Economics and Marketing
questions.stem: Gross margin is commonly approximated as:
questions.explanation: Gross margin ≈ returns minus variable costs.

questions.subject: Agricultural Economics and Marketing
questions.stem: An agricultural cooperative is primarily owned and controlled by:
questions.explanation: Coops are member-owned and member-controlled enterprises.

questions.subject: Agricultural Extension and Communication
questions.stem: Effective agricultural extension focuses on:
choices: One-way lectures only with no feedback
Facilitating learning and adoption through participatory communication with farmers
questions.explanation: Modern extension is participatory and learner-centered.

questions.subject: Agricultural Extension and Communication
questions.stem: A farmer field school primarily promotes learning through:
questions.explanation: FFS emphasizes discovery learning in the field.

questions.subject: Agricultural Extension and Communication
questions.stem: In diffusion of innovations, early adopters are typically:
choices: The very last to try anything
Opinion leaders who try innovations sooner than the majority
questions.explanation: Early adopters often influence later adopters.

questions.subject: Crop Science
questions.stem: Drip irrigation is advantageous because it:
choices: Applies water near the root zone and can improve efficiency
questions.explanation: Drip can reduce losses and target the root zone.

questions.subject: Soil Science
questions.stem: Contour farming helps reduce erosion mainly by:
choices: Following elevation contours to slow runoff
Increasing bare soil on slopes intentionally
questions.explanation: Contours slow water flow and reduce soil loss.

questions.subject: Crop Protection
questions.stem: A weed that germinates and completes its life cycle within one year is:
questions.explanation: Annuals complete life cycle in one year.

questions.subject: Animal Science
questions.stem: Biosecurity on livestock farms aims to:
choices: Prevent introduction and spread of pathogens
questions.explanation: Biosecurity reduces disease risk.

questions.subject: Agricultural Economics and Marketing
questions.stem: Value addition in agriculture can include:
choices: Processing, grading, packaging, and better market linkages
questions.explanation: Value addition improves marketability and returns.

questions.subject: Agricultural Extension and Communication
questions.stem: Gender-responsive extension recognizes that:
choices: Women and men may have different roles, access, and needs in agri-food systems
questions.explanation: Inclusive extension accounts for gendered roles and access.

questions.subject: Crop Science
questions.stem: El Niño in the Philippines commonly associates with:
choices: Higher risk of drought/drier conditions in many areas
questions.explanation: El Niño often brings drier conditions affecting PH agriculture.

questions.subject: Crop Science
questions.stem: Photosynthesis in crops primarily occurs in:
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts in green tissues drive photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Crop Science
questions.stem: Hybrid vigor (heterosis) refers to:
choices: Superior performance of hybrids relative to parents
questions.explanation: Heterosis is enhanced hybrid performance.

questions.subject: Soil Science
questions.stem: Nitrogen deficiency in plants often shows as:
choices: Overall chlorosis of older leaves first commonly
Purple stems only from excess N always
questions.explanation: N is mobile; older leaves yellow first commonly.

questions.subject: Soil Science
questions.stem: A soil pH of 7 is considered:
questions.explanation: pH 7 is neutral.

questions.subject: Crop Protection
questions.stem: Economic threshold is the pest density at which:
choices: Control measures should be taken to prevent reaching EIL
All insects must be eradicated always
questions.explanation: ET triggers action before economic injury level.

questions.subject: Crop Protection
questions.stem: A plant disease triangle includes host, pathogen, and:
questions.explanation: Disease requires susceptible host, pathogen, and conducive environment.

questions.subject: Animal Science
questions.stem: Roughages are generally higher in:
questions.explanation: Roughages are fibrous feeds.

questions.subject: Animal Science
questions.stem: Artificial insemination in livestock primarily aims to:
choices: Improve genetics and breeding efficiency with selected sires
questions.explanation: AI spreads superior genetics efficiently.

questions.subject: Agricultural Economics and Marketing
questions.stem: Other things equal, a bumper harvest that increases supply tends to:
questions.explanation: Increased supply typically lowers equilibrium price ceteris paribus.

questions.subject: Agricultural Economics and Marketing
questions.stem: An agricultural cooperative is owned by:
questions.explanation: Coops are member-owned enterprises.

questions.subject: Agricultural Extension and Communication
questions.stem: Farmer field schools emphasize:
choices: Participatory, experiential learning in the field
questions.explanation: FFS is participatory field-based learning.

questions.subject: Agricultural Extension and Communication
questions.stem: Relative advantage of an innovation refers to:
choices: How much better it is perceived vs. the idea it supersedes
questions.explanation: Relative advantage influences adoption speed.

questions.subject: Crop Science
questions.stem: Field capacity is roughly the soil water content after:
choices: Drainage of excess water following saturation
questions.explanation: Field capacity follows drainage of gravitational water.

questions.subject: Soil Science
questions.stem: Mulching helps reduce erosion by:
choices: Protecting the soil surface and reducing raindrop impact/runoff velocity
questions.explanation: Cover mulch protects soil and slows runoff.

questions.subject: Crop Protection
questions.stem: Integrated Pest Management combines:
choices: Multiple compatible tactics to manage pests economically and safely
questions.explanation: IPM integrates monitoring and multiple control tactics.

questions.subject: Animal Science
questions.stem: Vaccination programs primarily provide:
questions.explanation: Vaccines stimulate protective immunity.

questions.subject: Agricultural Economics and Marketing
questions.stem: Production loans for farmers are typically intended to finance:
choices: Inputs and operations for a production cycle
questions.explanation: Production credit funds crop/livestock operating needs.

questions.subject: Agricultural Extension and Communication
questions.stem: SMS advisories to farmers are an example of:
choices: Using ICT for timely agricultural information
questions.explanation: ICT channels deliver timely agri-info.

questions.subject: Crop Science
questions.stem: Drought-resilient varieties are bred mainly to:
questions.explanation: Drought resilience sustains performance under water stress.

questions.subject: Soil Science
questions.stem: Soil organic matter contributes to:
choices: Structure, nutrient cycling, and water holding capacity
Only soil color with no other role
questions.explanation: OM improves physical, chemical, and biological soil properties.

questions.subject: Crop Protection
questions.stem: A competitive crop canopy can reduce weeds by:
choices: Shading and resource competition against weeds
Removing all crop residues always for weeds’ benefit
questions.explanation: Canopy competition suppresses weeds.

questions.subject: Animal Science
questions.stem: Indigenous animal genetic resources are important because they often:
choices: Carry adaptation to local environments and systems
Are identical to all exotic breeds always
questions.explanation: Local breeds often adapt to local stressors and systems.

questions.subject: Agricultural Economics and Marketing
questions.stem: Reducing postharvest losses primarily increases:
choices: Food available from the same production
questions.explanation: Less loss means more food/income from same harvest.

questions.subject: Agricultural Extension and Communication
questions.stem: Collecting sex-disaggregated data in extension helps to:
choices: Design inclusive programs responsive to different roles/access
Serve only one gender always by default without analysis
questions.explanation: Sex-disaggregated data informs equitable programming.

questions.subject: Crop Science
questions.stem: Certified seed aims to provide:
choices: Genetic identity and quality standards assurance
questions.explanation: Certification assures varietal identity and quality attributes.
